newsitem.title: USA: Most natgas futures end up on technicals, cash.
newsitem.headline: Most natgas futures end up on technicals, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly ended higher Monday in a moderate session, boosted by a steady stream of technical buying and short covering on reports of firmer physical prices, sources said.
October rallied 10.9 cents to close at $1.973 per million British thermal units. November settled 9.5 cents higher at $2.167. Most others ended up by one-half to 7.2 cents.
"Today, cash moved over index, and some sellers were feeling the tide may be turning," said one Houston-based trader, adding the lack of selling plus short covering helped firm the complex today.

Traders also said the near forty-cent spread between cash and December NYMEX helped spur some up front buying for storage despite forecasts for mostly seasonal to below-seasonal U.S. weather this week.

Technically, traders noted October gapped higher today and broke some near-resistance points, making a run at psychological resistance at $2 a likely possibility near-term. Support was seen at the new gap at $1.88-1.885.
Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices gained a few cents Monday to the mid-to-high $1.80s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to about the $1.70 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 3.7 cents to $2.082. NYMEX said 35,743 Henry Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 30,880.
NYMEX October Permian natgas closed 11 cents higher at $1.64, while deferreds were untraded but settled up by five to eight cents. NYMEX said 16 Permian contracts traded.

On the KCBT, October finished eight cents higher at $1.75, while deferreds ended up by two to 6.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 2.9 cents to 22.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 286 lots traded, up from Friday's 155.
